# Independent functional audit: optimized convex-root majorants

Audited `candidate 3bbe467275a530f8`
in full. All finite-program, dual, and example statements pass.

* The vertex constraints of each representation polytope imply its complete
Jensen family by linearity in the representation. The convex-envelope
extension attains exactly the prescribed sampled values, is positive,
and handles deficient base dimension. Thus the value polyhedron is exact.
* The positive-part objective equals a maximum over finitely many subsets.
Commuting this finite maximum with the supremum gives the displayed formula.
For each subset, projection of the feasible polyhedron is closed and the
power objective is coercive on its positive lower-bounded coordinates, so
the asserted minima and hence the optimized objective are attained.
* Both dual signs agree with the constraints Dl<=0 and l>=r. The active
polyhedral normal cone argument gives multipliers even with dependent
Jensen equalities. Dotting the stationarity equation with the positive
optimizer gives eta.r=q V_A; the Young-conjugate term is exactly
(q-1)V_A. The q=1 branch and empty subset are separately correct.
* For the three-point profile, decreasing the middle majorant to b and
then the endpoint sum to 2b preserves feasibility and improves the
objective. In the both-active region the maximum is the balanced choice;
in the one-active region the smallest allowed endpoint a is feasible
whenever that region is nonempty and maximizes it. The zero-active region
adds nothing. This proves the exact formula in every q>=1, including
threshold equalities.
* The q=1 simplification, minimum ratio 5/7 at a=2b/3, direct width-(2,3,2)
certificate, and formal relaxed budget B=3/2 all check. The actual body is
centrally symmetric and has depth 1/2, so no low-depth or cap-cover claim
is being inferred from those scalar necessary conditions.
* Restriction to each binary-base copy proves the higher-n upper bound,
and an old-coordinate affine optimizer attains it. Positive combinations
of separate majorant inequalities retain their repeated factor mB and
cannot improve the supremum; the scope caveat about a genuinely new
cross-region geometric relation is justified.

No correction is needed.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
